title: Amazon Polly Pricing: Rates and Costs in 2026
summary: Amazon Polly pricing varies 25x by engine: Standard at $4, Neural at $16, Generative at $30, or Long-form at $100 per million characters.
body_markdown:
## What Polly costs at realistic monthly volumes


With the free tier set to zero and everything priced at the paid rate, Polly's monthly bill runs from 12 cents to $500 depending on workload and engine, so the actual cost can be computed from character volume.


The table uses $4, $16 and $100 per million characters for Standard, Neural and Long-form, and shows that **the engine barely matters until volume arrives** , making engine choice a decision you can defer.


Workload Characters per month Standard ($4/M) Neural ($16/M) Long-form ($100/M)


Blog narration 30,000 (4 posts × 7,500) 0.03 × 4 = $0.12 0.03 × 16 = $0.48 0.03 × 100 = $3.00


E-learning library 500,000 0.5 × 4 = $2 0.5 × 16 = $8 0.5 × 100 = $50


IVR 5,000,000 5 × 4 = $20 5 × 16 = $80 5 × 100 = $500


On the IVR row, the figures match[AWS's published pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/polly/pricing/) : $20, $80 or $500 for the same 5M characters, confirming the advertised rates hold up in practice. The last row is the one most worth arguing about on an invoice.


Even Long-form costs $3.00 on four posts of 7,500 characters, which is 30,000 characters a month.


That means no client will notice the difference between $0.12 and $3.00, and you should pick the engine on sound quality alone. Don't spend an hour on cost modelling for a workload this small.


### Polly pricing for e-learning and audiobooks


$50 on Long-form is still small, but it's 25 times the Standard figure, and it recurs if you regenerate the whole library every month, turning it into a significant recurring cost.


A 500,000-character library costs $2 on Standard and $8 on Neural, which means you can use this to estimate costs at other volumes.


Generate each lesson once, store the audio file, and serve it from storage. Then you pay for narration once, not on every playback or every re-render.


### Polly pricing for IVR and chatbot traffic


At five million characters a month, the bill is $20 on Standard, $80 on Neural and $500 on Long-form.


Choose Long-form for a phone menu and you add **$480 a month over Standard** , or $5,760 a year, for audio that callers hear in short fragments.


On a shared account, that gap quietly lands on whoever else is paying the AWS bill unless you bill it back to the IVR client.


> Choose Long-form for a phone menu and you add $480 a month over Standard, or $5,760 a year, for audio that callers hear in short fragments.


Because most IVR text is repetitive prompts such as greetings, menu options and confirmations, you can cache those, and only genuinely dynamic sentences reach Polly.


The same caller traffic can then cost a fraction of the table's figure, and that saving beats any plan or free tier.
